tasks.title: close-phase and the worktree tool name the commands that finish their work, and a group of phases on one branch can be signed off
tasks.description: Reproduced at HEAD: from the main worktree standing on the phase branch the merge lands, then the branch deletion says 'the worktree must go first' (impossible for the main tree) and the ownership refusal fires before the isMain check, telling the operator to git worktree remove the main tree. Check isMain before ownership; when the holder is the main tree print git switch <parent> and git branch -d <branch>; never move HEAD. A phase with phase.branch null is refused with 'whether audit/p1-p1 is contained could not be established' - say the name was composed because no branch is recorded and ask for --branch. Phases built on one combined branch: --branch already lands them; add a group sign-off (review from the task.commit lists, one gate, one invariants run over the union) in the signoff verb/command, reusing close-phase --branch per phase.

outcome.technical: cleanup_plan checks isMain first and main_tree_release prints the follow-ups; composed-name exit 4; signoff P1,P2 --branch --plan/--verdict via group_plan.
outcome.descriptive: close-phase tells the operator exactly what to run to finish from the main worktree, and phases built on one branch can be signed off together.

tasks.title: Review findings: the group gate owns the union, a group branch is never its own parent, and every commit on the branch is accounted for
tasks.description:
Phase review findings, all to be fixed, pre-existing 1 and 2 included (pre-existing 2: a --verdict passed on either path requires a current testEvidence for the phase, or an explicit recorded reason). Orchestrator decisions: the group's one gate run owns the UNION of the members' files (run-test-gate takes the group), the branch may never equal a member's parent (group_plan and close-phase resolve both refuse), every commit fork..branch is a member's recorded commit or is refused by name, non-carrier members carry a persistent record of what graded them that no-test-evidence and the report read, the invariants run sees branch/baseRef (record them first or re-run after), and the composed-name refusal is exit 1 (git answered; the command must change).
R1 (high) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5221-5234,5474-5477; plugins/audit/reference/phase-signoff.md:378-381: The group's one gate run only covers the carrier member's files, not the whole group. The printed command is `run-test-gate.py <manifest> <carrier> --record`, and run-test-gate works out what the run owns with `owned_files(manifest, carrier)` (run-test-gate.py:1936, used at :3573). That is the carrier's task files only, and three things are scoped by it. (a) The gate-mutated refusal: `attributed_mutations` (run-test-gate.py:372-391) refuses only on OWNED changes, so if the gate rewrites a file a non-carrier member owns, that change is only reported beside a `passed` verdict. (b) The coverage answer. (c) The `testedState` stamp (`tested_state(project, owns, ...)`, :2700). So phase-signoff.md:380 'The members share one tree, so one run measures all of them' is true of which commands run and false of what the run grades. Judged from reading the code; I did not run it. -> Give run-test-gate a group scope: accept a comma list of phases, or `--also <pid,...>`, so `owned_files` returns the union of every member's task files. Have `_print_group_plan` print that spelling. Add a case where the gate rewrites a file only a non-carrier member owns, and prove it reads `gate-mutated` (red on the current code). Until then, have the doc say which answers the one run is scoped to.
R2 (high) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5236-5314 (group_plan), :5322-5331 (landing_commands): Nothing refuses a `--branch` that is the members' resolved parent, e.g. `signoff P1,P2 --branch main` for phases whose work was committed straight onto main. Every task commit is CONTAINED in main, `merge-base main main` gives a fork, and no refusal fires. The record then writes `phase.branch = main`, and the last printed landing is `close-phase.py ... --branch main` without `--keep-branch`. In close-phase that case is already-contained and settled. If main is checked out nowhere, `cleanup_plan` then plans `update-ref -d refs/heads/main <sha>` (_worktrees.py:1061-1066), which deletes the development branch and its reflog. If the main tree holds main, the new follow-up prints `git switch main` and then `git branch -d main`, which git refuses. Judged from reading; not run. -> In group_plan, refuse when `branch` equals any member's resolved parent: 'a group branch is not its own parent'. Add a gs case (red first) where `--branch` is the parent. The same guard belongs in close-phase `resolve()`; see preExisting 1.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5262-5270,5298-5303: The review is scoped to the members' `task.commit` list, and each listed commit is checked to be ON the branch. Nothing checks the other direction: which commits the branch carries beyond those. Another phase's work, a hand fix-up or a stray commit between `fork` and the branch tip is neither in the printed review scope nor refused. It still lands, because the first `close-phase --branch` merges the whole branch. So a group can record a `passed` verdict and land work nobody reviewed, including work from a phase that is not in the group and not signed off. -> Compute `git rev-list <fork>..<branch>`. Refuse, naming each one, any commit that is neither a member's `task.commit` nor an audit-state/index commit the journal records for a member. Or print those commits under 'not in any member - not reviewed' and make the record refuse while any remain. Add a case with an unrecorded commit on the branch.
R4 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5378-5391,5450-5451; plugins/audit/reference/phase-signoff.md:380-381: Nothing persistent records that the non-carrier members were graded by the carrier's run. The only statement is one stdout line: 'the others carry no testEvidence of their own'. Once they land, `/audit:status --gate --fail-on no-test-evidence` will name them as 'done subject(s) with no run recorded' (_status_facts / audit-status.py:1402), and its repair is to run their gate, which defeats the one-run design. The report and panel show a passed phase with no evidence. The record also never checks that the carrier has a gate row on this tree, which matches the single-phase path but means the group verdict can be written before any gate ran. -> At record time, require the carrier's `testEvidence` (status passed or empty-gate). Write to each non-carrier member either the same pointer or a field such as `review.gradedBy: <carrierId>` that `no-test-evidence` and the report read as evidence. Check the pointer against doctor's pointer-vs-ledger check (_doctor_completions.py:125) so it does not read as a mismatch. Add cases for both.

So at the sign-off's only invariants run the members have no branch and no baseRef. `base_ref` and `branch_history` (_invariants.py:793,1170) then do not apply, and the group gets fewer checks than a single-phase sign-off, which has both from `start`. Nothing says the sign-off's own run skipped those checks. -> Either record branch/baseRef before step 3, as a separate write or a `--plan` side-effect that is refused later if the group changes, or add a step-4b invariants re-run after the record. Otherwise have the plan output say that base-ref and branch-history are not graded at this sign-off.

tasks.title: Second-review findings: one verdict-binding rule serves commit and sign-off, reused runs bind through their source, and gradedBy is shown
tasks.description:
Second phase review findings, all to be fixed. RUN ONLY AFTER P71 HAS LANDED and main is merged into this branch: (R1, R2) there is ONE verdict-binding rule - P71's commit-task-work verdict_binding (reused rows graded through reusedFrom, recorder paths excluded, gate-mismatch, unanswerable, newest row for the subject) - moved into a library module both commit-task-work and signoff call; evidence_refusal is deleted, not patched. (R3) report and panel render gradedBy; the schema documents gradedBy and review.noEvidenceReason and its testEvidence description is made true. (R4) a recorded --accept <sha> --reason escape for a legitimate unrecorded commit, merge commits whose parents are accounted for are accounted, and a missing task commit names repair-commits.py. R5-R12 as the review says.
R1 (high) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5117-5160 (evidence_refusal); plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py:2248-2280 (reused_result), :3656-3661, :3694: When the gate verdict is reused, `signoff --verdict passed` is refused on both paths, and the refusal sentence is false. Reuse is the gate's default. A reused run is recorded as a NEW row with a new runId, and the phase pointer moves to that row. `reused_result` carries no `testedState`, so the row's `testedState` is `{}`. `evidence_refusal` reads `row[-1].testedState.scopeDigest` as None and compares it with the live digest. For any phase that declares files, that comparison fails and prints 'is not current: ... they have changed since', even though nothing changed. The printed remedy (`run-test-gate.py ... --record`) reuses again, so the operator loops. The only way out is `--no-reuse`, which the refusal never names. A second phase-scope run on an unchanged tree reuses: `/audit:review` re-running a sign-off, a sign-off retried after another refusal, or a pointer that was refused and then re-run. So this breaks exactly the flows in question 1. Every new case (gs_gate, gse1/gse2, so12/so13) runs the gate with `--no-reuse`, so no case reaches this path. Judged from reading; not run. -> Grade a repeated row against the run that measured it. Follow `reusedFrom.runId` to that row, and refuse only when the source is missing from the ledger. P71's `commit-task-work.verdict_binding` already implements that rule (see finding 2). Add a red-first case: gate once with `--no-reuse`, gate again WITHOUT it, then `signoff --verdict passed` must exit 0. Also add the other direction: a reused row whose source was removed from the ledger is refused.
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5117-5160 (evidence_refusal) vs audit/p71-a-task-commit-carries-what-the:plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-task-work.py:477-640 (verdict_binding/_digest_binding): `evidence_refusal` is a second implementation of 'does this recorded verdict bind the declared work now'. P71, a sibling phase of the same wave, already built that rule for task commits, and this copy has fewer arms. (a) It does not exclude recorder-written paths. P71 changes `scope_digest`/`tested_state` to take `excluded=recorded_paths(...)`, and the recorder will then store an excluded digest while this caller computes an unexcluded one. Once both land, any phase that declares the manifest, journal or evidence path is refused for ever. On this tree that is already true, because `write_pointer` rewrites the shard after the digest is taken. (b) It has no gate-mismatch arm. An `empty-gate` pointer, which is never checked for currency, or a `passed` pointer taken under an older `testGate` is accepted after `/audit:phase retarget --gate` widens the gate. So `retarget --gate-clear`, run, `retarget --gate lint`, then `signoff --verdict passed` records a pass that no run backs. (c) It has no reused-row arm (finding 1) and no unanswerable arm. (d) It reads the pointer rather than the newest row for the subject. -> Move one binding function into a shared module (`_evidence_io` or `_tree_stamp`). It should take (rows, subject ids, gate entries, files, excluded) and return bound/refused with a sentence. Call it from both `commit-task-work` and `signoff`, and reconcile with P71 before either lands. Add cases for a declared manifest path, a gate changed after an empty-gate run, and a reused row.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/report/_evidence_view.py:120-149; plugins/audit/scripts/ui/panel/overview.js:400-420; plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_composition.py:683-697; plugins/audit/schema/audit-plan.schema.json ($defs/testEvidence); plugins/audit/reference/phase-signoff.md:398-401: The report and the panel render a non-carrier member's copied pointer as that phase's OWN sign-off run. `_evidence_view._view_for` looks up the runId and renders it as `phases[pid].own`, which its own docstring keeps apart 'because merging them would claim a measurement nobody made'. The panel's `evState` does the same. `gradedBy` has no renderer anywhere; grep finds readers only in `_status_facts.graded_by`, whose own comment warns that 'a surface rendering it as the member's run would claim a gate nobody ran'. That is exactly what both surfaces do. So phase-signoff.md:400 'the report read[s] it as graded, by that run' is true of 'graded' and false of 'by that run'. The schema also leaves `gradedBy` and `review.noEvidenceReason` undocumented. Its testEvidence description says 'deleting it is always safe ... the next run writes it back', which is false for a copy: `reconcile` walks ledger subjects only and never restores a member's copied pointer. -> Render `gradedBy` in `tev_view`/`_view_for` and in the panel's evidence badge, for example 'graded by P1's run <id>'. Add `gradedBy` (and `review.noEvidenceReason`) to the schema with their meaning. Amend the testEvidence description to name the one pointer the ledger cannot re-derive. Add a report pin and a browser-gate assertion for a gradedBy phase.
R4 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5395-5413 (group_plan stray check): The accounting has no route for a legitimate commit that no member records, so a group that carries one cannot be signed off at all. The only repair is rewriting the branch, which this repo forbids ('Never rebase', 'fix forward'). Three cases reach it. (1) Merge commits: a combined branch built by merging the phase branches, or one that merged its parent back in, has merge commits in `fork..branch` that no task or audit-state commit is. (2) Hand-made journal-only or planning commits: this repo makes them, e.g. main's 46570889 'chore(audit-state): journal rows the session's hook wrote' and the multi-phase planning commit 386e6637. Neither has an `audit.state.committed` row naming a member. (3) A rebased branch: task commits are refused as not on the branch (correct), and the refusal does not name `repair-commits.py`. rev-list's cost is not the problem; it is linear in the commits and the match loop is small. -> Add an explicit, recorded escape, e.g. `--accept <sha>` with a reason written to each member's review and printed in the review scope, so the commit is reviewed rather than hidden. Consider treating a merge commit whose parents are all accounted-for or parent-side as accounted. When a recorded task commit is missing from the branch, name `repair-commits.py`. Add cases: a merge-built combined branch, and a journal-only commit.

Every audit-state and index commit then reads as stray, and the refusal blames the commits ('no member records') instead of saying the journal could not be read. That is a missing basis presented as a finding about the branch. -> Carry the read failure into group_plan and emit it as its own refusal line ('the journal could not be read, so audit-state commits could not be accounted: <exc>'). Add a case.

(c) Doctor's recovery for a merged-but-unsigned phase and the panel's sign-off-due note both name `/audit:phase signoff <id>` as the step that 'records the verdict that reads it done', with no gate run. For a `passed` verdict that step now refuses. -> In step 5a, state the evidence requirement and the flag. tasks.title: Round-3 review findings: a group run is never a reused solo run, a merge carrying its own content is reviewed, and group-only flags are refused on one phase
tasks.description:
Round-3 phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (R1) the members a run covers (groupWith) are part of the reuse identity, so a group run never reuses a solo run; the refusal names the exact command that satisfies it; ve7 runs that command and reaches sign-off. (R2) a merge commit is accounted only when its tree equals the automatic merge of its parents (git merge-tree --write-tree); a merge carrying its own content is listed for review and refused unless --accept names it; the docs stop asserting it carries no work and say what is checked. (R3) the group-only flags (--bind, --accept, --reason with --accept) on a single-phase sign-off are refused with a usage error that names the group form, before anything is written. (R4) --accept resolves through git rev-parse to one full commit on the branch and refuses an ambiguous or unknown prefix. (R5) an empty carrier gate refuses the group binding instead of copying an old run. (R6) review.acceptedCommits is shown in the report's sign-off note and the panel's. (R7) the commit message is history and stays; the prose counts it points at (COMPATIBILITY 'gained two', the schema's 'ONE exception') are reworded to carry no count. (R8) the coverage basis of a group run names the members whose files it covers.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6369-6388 (_group_binding); plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py:2200-2238 (reuse_identity), :3547-3551: The group gate can loop on reuse, the same class as R1. `groupWith` is not part of the reuse identity, which is content + gate + declared_scope(owns). When a member's files are a subset of the carrier's, the union equals the carrier's own files. A solo carrier run (`run-test-gate P1 --record`) is then reused by the group run the refusal prints (`run-test-gate P1 --also P2 --record`, with no --no-reuse). `_group_binding` grades the reused row through `reusedFrom` to the solo origin, which has no `groupWith`, so it refuses again with 'owned P1 alone, not P2 - run `...--also P2 --record`'. Re-running that command reuses again, and the refusal never names --no-reuse. I RAN this with the real scripts: P2.files=[src/p1.py], solo gate --no-reuse exit 0, group gate exit 0 printing 'GATE VERDICT REUSED ... from run 020b9c', then `signoff P1,P2 --branch combined --verdict passed` exited 2 with 'the run that measured it (...020b9c) owned P1 alone, not P2'. Case ve7 stops at the first refusal and never runs the printed remedy. -> Put the owned member set (`also`, sorted) into the reuse identity key, so a group run never repeats a solo run or the reverse. Alternatively, grade `groupWith` on the repeating row when its origin's owned file set is identical, and name --no-reuse in the refusal. Add a case continuing ve7: run the printed command WITHOUT --no-reuse, then signoff must exit 0 (red today).
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6224-6246 (_account), :6100-6104 (group_plan docstring); plugins/audit/reference/phase-signoff.md ('a branch built by merging the members' own branches is made of them'): A merge commit is accounted whenever its parents are accounted, and nothing checks the merge's OWN content. The docstring says such a merge 'carries no work of its own', but that is never checked. An evil merge, or a conflict resolution, lands unreviewed. It is not listed in the step-2 review scope (only task commits and accepted ones are), yet the first landing merges it. I RAN this: side1 (P1.1) and side2 (P2.1) were merged --no-ff into combined, and the second merge added backdoor.py (`git show --cc --stat` shows 'backdoor.py | 1 +'). `signoff P1,P2 --branch combined --plan` exited 0 and listed only the two task commits for review. -> Account a merge only when `git diff-tree --cc -p <merge>` (or `git show --cc --format= <merge>`) is empty, meaning a clean merge carries nothing of its own. Otherwise treat it as stray, or list every merge in the review scope as `git show --cc <sha>`. Add a case: a merge with its own hunk is refused (or listed), and ga4's clean merges stay accounted.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:5858-5860 (cmd_signoff dispatch), :6282-6314 (_group_door): The group-only flags are accepted and ignored on the single-phase path. The dispatch sends only `len(ids)>1 or --branch or --plan` to `_group_door`, so its own refusals ('--plan and --bind are a group sign-off's, which needs --branch'; '--accept needs --reason') are unreachable for `--bind`, `--accept` and `--reason` on one phase. I RAN these: `signoff P1 --bind` exits 2 with 'needs --verdict', which steers the operator toward a verdict. `signoff P1 --bind --verdict skipped --summary s` exits 0 and writes an irreversible sign-off. `signoff P1 --verdict passed ... --accept deadbeef --reason r` exits 0 and records nothing of the accept. This is the 'flag accepted and ignored' class this file's own flag table warns about. -> Add `args.bind or args.accept or (args.reason or '').strip()` to the dispatch condition, so `_group_door` refuses them without --branch. Or refuse them explicitly on the single path. Add cases for `signoff P1 --bind` and `signoff P1 --accept x --reason r --verdict skipped`, both exit 2 with nothing written.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6224-6246 (_account, `named = [a for a in accepted if _is_accounted(sha, [a])]`), :6218-6219 (_is_accounted): One --accept value takes in every commit whose SHA starts with it, with no length floor and no uniqueness check. I RAN this: 12 stray commits, `--accept 1 --reason r`, and 3 of them (every SHA starting with '1') were taken into the group, leaving 9 refused. Each accepted SHA is listed in full in the plan, so nothing is hidden, but one flag the operator meant for one commit can accept several, each recorded with that one reason. -> Resolve each --accept with `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`, or require it to match exactly one commit in fork..branch. Refuse an ambiguous or short value by name.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6383-6388 (_group_binding no-gate return), :6420-6421, :6462: When the carrier's gate declares no entry (state `no-gate`), the carrier's newest row is still copied onto every member as `gradedBy`, and that row may be any older run. I RAN this: P1 was measured solo under [test], then P1's testGate was cleared, then `signoff P1,P2 --branch combined --verdict passed` exited 0. It printed 'gate: the group's one run is P1's; P2 records it as its own, gradedBy P1', and P2.testEvidence became P1's old solo run. That run never owned P2 (no groupWith) and was taken under a gate that no longer exists. -> In the `no-gate` state, copy no pointer and print the existing 'declares no entry, so the sign-off rests on review alone' line. Alternatively, copy only an `empty-gate` row that carries `groupWith` for every member.
R6 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6452-6454 (review.acceptedCommits); report/_evidence_view.py; ui/panel/overview.js: `review.acceptedCommits` is written on every member and read by nothing: grep finds only the writer, the schema, the demo exemption and ga3. R8 raised the same class for noEvidenceReason. A commit taken into a group's review outside every task is exactly what a later reader of the report needs to see, and it is visible only in the --plan output of the session that ran it. -> Render acceptedCommits (sha and reason) beside the sign-off verdict in the report and the panel. Or state in phase-signoff.md that it is a record without a reader.
R7 (low) commit afd72d91 message (audit-stamp line, claim 7): R12 asked for stamp-verification stamps. The message carries `audit-stamp: head dcb72589, scopeDigest sha256:211cfee...`, which is not the tool's JSON. `stamp-verification.py compare --stamp-file <message>` refuses it with 'the text after audit-stamp: is not JSON', so the claim cannot be graded. The JSON stamp in the executor's scratch (p74c/stamp.txt) has a different scopeDigest (ba8e239e...) and grades `stale` against this worktree now. Claim 7, 'no count written into prose by this change', sits beside COMPATIBILITY.md's 'gained one additive key ... gained two' and the schema's 'with ONE exception'. Those are enumerated and arguably historical, but the claim as written is not true. -> Paste the JSON line `stamp-verification.py take` prints, taken on the committed tree. Reword claim 7 to 'no count without its enumeration or command beside it'.
R8 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py:1925-1930 (coverage basis): R9's second half is still open. The group row now records `groupWith`, but its coverage basis still lists other members' files as 'declared but not named by the run', with no word that they are the group's members' files and not the carrier's declaration. -> When `also` is set, label those files by their owning member in the coverage basis, e.g. 'declared by P2 (group member)'.

tasks.title: Round-4 review findings: a merge the tool cannot recompute is said so, the printed review command shows what was refused, and --accept takes a SHA only
tasks.description:
Round-4 phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (U1) _clean_merge answers three states - clean (merge-tree exit 0 and equal tree), own content (merge-tree exit 1, or a differing tree), and could-not-ask (any other exit, carrying git's own error line and naming the git 2.38 requirement); could-not-ask is a refusal with that honest reason, never 'an edit', and --accept still takes the commit in; a case under a PATH shim that behaves like old git. (U2) the review command printed for a refused merge is the comparison the check made: git diff <tree of git merge-tree --write-tree p1 p2> <sha>, which shows a dropped change that git show --cc hides; ga8b is renamed to what it asserts and a case proves the printed command shows the dropped change. (U3) an octopus merge is could-not-ask with the reason that merge-tree recomputes two parents only. (U4) an accepted commit counts as accounted when the merges above it are judged, and a merge whose only unaccounted parent is a refused merge is listed as waiting on that SHA, not as 'no member records'. (U5) --accept takes a hex SHA or unique hex prefix only (a ref name or revision expression is refused by name), resolved to the full SHA recorded. (U6) a vitest case for the done-phase accepted-commits note.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6252-6268 (_clean_merge), :6212-6218 (the 'carries content of its own' refusal): When git cannot answer, the refusal gives a false reason. `_clean_merge` returns False for every non-zero exit from `git merge-tree --write-tree`. That covers git older than 2.38, which has no --write-tree: git 2.37 parses it as a base rev and dies with 'unknown rev --write-tree', exit 128. It also covers a missing object in a shallow clone. False is then reported as 'its tree is not the automatic merge of its parents, so it is a conflict resolution or an edit no task records'. I RAN this through a PATH shim that reproduces the old-git failure (scratchpad/p74r3/oldgit/git, r4b.py). A branch built from two clean --no-ff merges, which gets `--plan` exit 0 on git 2.50.1, got exit 2 under the shim. The refusal called merge m1 an edit, and listed the clean merge m2 above it as a commit 'no member records'. The repo already knows about this floor: `_merge_install.py:225-241` says '`merge-tree --write-tree` needs git 2.38+', and `test__worktrees.py:192` names Ubuntu 22.04, whose git (2.34) is older than that. CLAUDE.md's rule applies: when the basis is missing, say that. -> Make `_clean_merge` answer one of three states: clean; own (exit 1 means conflicted, or the tree differs); could-not-ask (any other exit, carrying stderr's first line). A could-not-ask merge gets its own refusal, e.g. 'whether merge X carries content of its own could not be asked (`git merge-tree --write-tree`: <stderr>; needs git 2.38+)'. Take the version wording from `_merge_install`. Add a case that injects a run fn returning exit 128 for merge-tree, and check the sentence is the could-not-ask one.
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:6212-6218 (refusal names `git show --cc <sha>`), :6667 (plan lists `accepted  git show <sha>`); plugins/audit/reference/phase-signoff.md:402-405; plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py ga8b: The detection works, but the review command it prints does not show what it detected. I RAN r4c.py: during a clean merge of side2 I ran `git rm -f src/p2.py`, which silently dropped side2's change. `--plan` correctly refused merge a1afcbc0700e. But both `git show --cc <sha>`, which the refusal names, and `git show --format= <sha>`, which the plan lists for an accepted commit, print NOTHING. A dense combined diff hides any path whose result equals one parent. `git show --remerge-diff <sha>` shows the deletion. So a reviewer who follows the printed step sees an empty diff and passes --accept. Separately, ga8b's name says 'listed with `git show --cc`', but it asserts that plain `git show <sha>` is in the output. -> For a merge, name `git show --remerge-diff <sha>` (git 2.36+), or `git diff <merge-tree tree> <sha>` from the tree `_clean_merge` already computed. tasks.title: close-phase writes the landing stamp into the copy that survives, whatever manifest path it is given
tasks.description: Reported while landing P78: `close-phase.py <wt>/docs/audit/audit-plan.json P78 --project <wt> --dry-run` printed "cleanup is not finished. From <main>, run: close-phase.py <wt>/docs/audit/audit-plan.json P78 --project .". Run as printed from main, it merged with --ff-only, then wrote mergedAt and the derived status into the WORKTREE's shard and re-mirrored the WORKTREE's index stub - the copy removed moments later - so the worktree removal refused on those writes, while its phase.merged journal row went into MAIN's journal. The rule: the landing stamp is written to the manifest of the tree the merge lands in (the parent branch's checkout), never to a copy inside the phase's own worktree, whatever path is passed; and the dry-run's follow-up command names that surviving manifest. Red-first: close-phase given the worktree's manifest from the main checkout writes nothing under the worktree, stamps main's copies, and the worktree removal succeeds; plus the printed follow-up names main's manifest.

tasks.title: run-test-gate's crowd line counts only runs that truly shared a window, not one that started the second the last one ended
tasks.description: Reported while recording P79's wave-3 task gates (runs 15:49:37Z.28e86c, 15:50:39Z.3d1d04, 15:51:38Z.ea5bd0): the crowd line "N other gate run(s) shared this window" fires on runs recorded strictly one after the other. `_evidence_io._overlaps` is inclusive at both endpoints while `ts` and `startedAt` are whole seconds, so a run that starts in the same second the previous row was written always counts as overlapping. Decide overlap so that a run which began when the other had already ended does not count: compare half-open at the end (a run ending at second t and one starting at t are sequential), and where the rows carry sub-second or ordering evidence use it; if whole-second data cannot tell, say that in the line rather than asserting a shared window. Red-first both directions: back-to-back runs are not a crowd; two runs whose windows genuinely overlap by a second or more still are.
